tldr: Headlines across 12 buckets almost universally lead with the mass delegate walkout as the central fact, positioning Netanyahu's UNGA appearance as a diplomatic isolation event rather than a substantive address. The sole headline outlier is the Daily Wire, which ignores the walkout entirely and recasts the New York street protests as an anti-American act, while Daily Sabah is the only outlet to apply the word 'humiliating' in its title.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only headline in the corpus that makes no reference to the walkout or Netanyahu's speech; 'The America Haters Have A New Career Plan' reframes the New York street protest as an anti-American act, the sole outlet to omit the UN diplomatic event entirely from its title.

The only headline to apply the word 'humiliating' directly to Netanyahu's visit and name Israeli 'isolation' as the story's takeaway — stronger editorial characterisation than any other outlet's title.
'Netanyahu Faces an UNGA Walkout (Again)' is the only headline to note the walkout is a recurrence, framing the event as a pattern rather than a one-off diplomatic protest.
The only headline to report the counter-fact — that Malawi's delegation explicitly skipped the walkout and stayed in the chamber — inverting the dominant narrative of unified African condemnation.
Sole headline to name Iceland's FM and foreground the 'moral cowards' rebuttal, centring a small NATO state's diplomatic pushback rather than the walkout itself.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, the delegate walkout eclipses Netanyahu's speech content across every bucket except the US conservative outlet, where the New York street protest is recast as anti-American sentiment rather than pro-Palestinian dissent.
